\[
k \sim \operatorname{Poisson}\Bigl(\frac{I\, P}{255}\Bigr),
\qquad
I_{\text{out}} = \frac{255\, k}{P}
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(P\): The photon count at white
- \(k\): The random photon count

P is the photon count at white. The value I is turned into a mean photon count, a random count k is drawn with that mean, and k is scaled back to 0 to 255. A Poisson count with mean lambda has variance lambda, so the noise standard deviation in levels is the square root of 255 I / P. Bright areas get more noise in levels, but less relative to their value.
